To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified 111 different polymorphisms in the human DNA methyltransferase genes DNMT1, DNAM3A, DNAM3B, DNAM3L and DNAM2 (TRDM1).

(1) we identified a rare variant in DNMT3L that affects its ability to stimulate DNMT3A-mediated de novo DNA methyla- tion, and (2) this rare variant is associated with hypomethylation at a subset of CpG islands in subtelomeric regions.
a rare polymorphism in DNMT3L is associated with subtelomic DNA hypomethlyation in healthy individuals and that this polymorphism is predicted to affect DNMT3L protein function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a rare variant in DNMT3L that is associated with a specific hypomethylation profile.
the first systematic analysis of polymorphisms in human DNA methyltransferase genes.
the identification of genetic variation in DNMTs and its impact on DNA methylation profiles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the contribution of genetic variations in DNMT genes to inter-individual variation in DNA methylation is negligible, with the exception of a rare DNMTL variant that is associated with hypomethylation of repetitive subtelomeric CpG islands.
the contribution of polymorphisms in DNMT genes to inter-individual variation in DNA methylation is limited.
genetic variation in DNMTs does not play a major role in inter-individual variations of DNA methylation profiles in the healthy population.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a rare variant in DNMT3L is associated with hypomethylation of subtelomeric regions in healthy individuals.
the majority of polymorphisms detected in DNMT genes do not affect DNA methylation, but a rare DNMT polymorphism can lead to a significant hypomethylation at subtelomeric regions.
genetic variation in DNMTs is not a major contributor to the inter-individual variation in DNA methylation in normal populations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DNMT3L R271Q variant, which was associated with hypomethylation of subtelomeric CpG islands, may have a role in the inter-individual variation in DNA methylation patterns.
rare polymorphisms in DNMT3L may contribute to inter-individual variations of DNA methylation at repetitive genomic regions.
rare polymorphisms in DNMT3L are associated with subtelomic hypomethylation, which may have functional consequences.
